48. const ORDER: Ordering = Ordering::Relaxed;
49.

51. // Global Variables
52. //==================================================================================================

54. /// Physical memory manager storage.
55. static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER: MaybeUninit<PhysMemoryManager> = MaybeUninit::uninit();
56. 
57. /// Whether the physical memory manager has been initialized.

59.

65. /// # Description
66. ///
67. /// Physical memory manager.
68. ///

70. pub struct PhysMemoryManager {
71.     upool: Upool,
72. }
73.

75. // Implementations
76. //==================================================================================================
77. 
78. impl PhysMemoryManager {
79.     ///
80.     /// # Description
81.     ///
82.     /// Initializes the physical memory manager singleton.
83.     ///
84.     /// # Parameters
85.     ///
86.     /// - `upool`: User page pool.
87.     ///
88.     /// # Errors
89.     ///
90.     /// Returns `InvalidArgument` if the singleton has already been initialized.
91.     ///
92.     // Trusted shim: writes the `static mut` singleton storage and an `AtomicBool`
93.     // lifecycle gate (raw global state Verus cannot model). The manager-singleton
94.     // lifecycle flag is distinct from the frame-allocator lifecycle and has no
95.     // abstract model (the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` only tracks the allocator);
96.     // the contract therefore states the caller-relevant guarantee: the global
97.     // frame allocator stays initialized and well-formed across this call.
98.     #[allow(verus_impl_method_marker)]
99.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
100.     #[verus_spec(result =>
101.         requires
102.             phys_view().initialized,
103.             phys_view().inv(),
104.         ensures
105.             phys_view().inv(),
106.             phys_view().initialized,
107.     )]

110.             return Err(Error::new(
111.                 ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
112.                 "physical memory manager already initialized",
113.             ));
114.         }
115. 
116.         // SAFETY: this happens during kernel initialization and no other threads are running.
117.         unsafe { PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER.write(PhysMemoryManager { upool }) };
118.         PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT.store(true, ORDER);
119.         Ok(())
120.     }

124.     ///
125.     /// Gets a mutable reference to the physical memory manager.

127.     /// # Panics
128.     ///
129.     /// Panics if the physical memory manager is not initialized.
130.     ///
131.     /// # Safety
132.     ///
133.     /// This function is unsafe because it returns a mutable reference to a global variable.
134.     ///
135.     /// The caller must ensure:
136.     ///

141.     ///
142.     pub unsafe fn get_mut<'a>() -> &'a mut PhysMemoryManager {
143.         if unlikely(!PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT.load(ORDER)) {

151.     ///
152.     /// # Description
153.     ///
154.     /// Allocates user frames into caller-provided storage.
155.     ///
156.     /// The returned frames are not guaranteed to be physically contiguous.
157.     /// User allocations are gated by the kernel watermark: if fulfilling the request would
158.     /// leave fewer than `KERNEL_WATERMARK` free frames, the allocation is rejected.
159.     ///
160.     /// # Parameters
161.     ///
162.     /// - `count`: Number of frames to allocate.
163.     /// - `frames`: Mutable reference to a pre-allocated vector into which to store those
164.     ///   frames' addresses. It should have sufficient capacity for `count` entries.
165.     ///
166.     /// # Return Values
167.     ///
168.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned and `frames` is filled with `count` frames. Upon failure, an
169.     /// error is returned and any frames allocated by this call are dropped by truncating `frames`
170.     /// back to empty.
171.     ///
172.     // Trusted shim: loops over the global frame allocator (`Upool::alloc`) and the
173.     // caller-provided `Vec`, with `error!`-logging and a clear()-on-error rollback
174.     // that Verus cannot body-verify without editing exec code. The contract is
175.     // stated over `phys_view()` and `frames@`: on success exactly `count` frames
176.     // are handed out (each now allocated); on error the vector is emptied
177.     // (all-or-nothing). Frames are not claimed contiguous.
178.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
179.     #[verus_spec(result =>
180.         requires
181.             phys_view().initialized,
182.             phys_view().inv(),
183.             old(frames)@.len() == 0,
184.         ensures
185.             phys_view().inv(),
186.             phys_view().initialized,
187.             match result {
188.                 Ok(()) => {
189.                     &&& final(frames)@.len() == count
190.                     &&& forall|i: int|
191.                         0 <= i < count as int ==>
192.                             #[trigger] phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
193.                 },
194.                 Err(_) => final(frames)@.len() == 0,
195.             },
196.     )]
197.     pub fn alloc_many_user_frames(
198.         &mut self,
199.         count: usize,
200.         frames: &mut Vec<UserFrame>,
201.     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
202.         if !frames.is_empty() {
203.             let reason: &str = "frames vector is not empty";
204.             error!("{reason}");
205.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
206.         }
207.         if frames.capacity() < count {
208.             let reason: &str = "frames vector has insufficient capacity";
209.             error!("{reason}");
210.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
211.         }
212. 
213.         // A zero-sized allocation is trivially satisfied.
214.         if count == 0 {
215.             return Ok(());
216.         }
217. 
218.         Self::check_user_watermark(count)?;
219. 
220.         for _ in 0..count {
221.             match self.upool.alloc() {
222.                 Ok(frame) => frames.push(frame),
223.                 Err(error) => {
224.                     frames.clear();
225.                     return Err(error);
226.                 },
227.             }
228.         }
229.         Ok(())
230.     }

232.     ///
233.     /// # Description
234.     ///
235.     /// Allocates a single user frame, applying the same kernel watermark check as
236.     /// [`Self::alloc_many_user_frames`]. This is the single-frame fast path used on
237.     /// hot paths such as copy-on-write fault resolution, where allocating an
238.     /// intermediate [`Vec`] would be wasteful.
239.     ///
240.     /// # Returns
241.     ///
242.     /// Upon success, a [`UserFrame`] is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned
243.     /// instead.
244.     ///
245.     // Trusted shim: applies the watermark gate then delegates to the global
246.     // `Upool::alloc`. On success the returned frame's physical address is now in
247.     // the allocator's `allocated_frames` and is page-aligned.
248.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
249.     #[verus_spec(result =>
250.         requires
251.             phys_view().initialized,
252.             phys_view().inv(),
253.         ensures
254.             phys_view().inv(),
255.             phys_view().initialized,
256.             match result {
257.                 Ok(frame) => {
258.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
259.                     &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
260.                 },
261.                 Err(_) => true,
262.             },
263.     )]
264.     pub fn alloc_user_frame(&mut self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
265.         Self::check_user_watermark(1)?;
266.         self.upool.alloc()
267.     }

269.     ///
270.     /// # Description
271.     ///
272.     /// Rejects user allocations of `count` frames that would breach the kernel
273.     /// watermark, i.e. that would drop the number of free frames below
274.     /// [`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`].
275.     ///
276.     /// # Parameters
277.     ///
278.     /// - `count`: Number of user frames the caller intends to allocate.
279.     ///
280.     /// # Returns
281.     ///
282.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
283.     ///
284.     // Trusted shim: reads the global free-frame count and compares it against
285.     // `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`. Pure gate, no allocator state change. `Ok` exactly
286.     // captures the watermark policy: at least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames remain free
287.     // after servicing `count`. `Err` covers both the overflow guard and a breach.
288.     #[allow(verus_impl_method_marker)]
289.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
290.     #[verus_spec(result =>
291.         requires
292.             phys_view().initialized,
293.             phys_view().inv(),
294.         ensures
295.             phys_view().inv(),
296.             phys_view().initialized,
297.             phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite(),
298.             match result {
299.                 Ok(()) => spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, count as int),
300.                 Err(_) => true,
301.             },
302.     )]
303.     fn check_user_watermark(count: usize) -> Result<(), Error> {
304.         let watermark_threshold: usize = config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK
305.             .checked_add(count)
306.             .ok_or_else(|| {
307.                 let reason: &str = "watermark + count overflow";
308.                 error!("{reason}");
309.                 Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
310.             })?;
311.         if frame::free_count() < watermark_threshold {
312.             let reason: &str = "would breach kernel watermark";
313.             error!("{reason}");
314.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::OutOfMemory, reason));
315.         }
316.         Ok(())
317.     }
318. 
319.     ///
320.     /// # Description
321.     ///
322.     /// Allocates a kernel frame.
323.     ///
324.     /// Kernel allocations bypass the watermark — no artificial ceiling.
325.     ///
326.     /// # Return Values
327.     ///
328.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
329.     ///
330.     // Trusted shim: allocates one frame from the global allocator (bypassing the
331.     // watermark) and wraps it, freeing the raw frame if wrapping fails. On success
332.     // the returned frame's base address is now allocated and page-aligned.
333.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
334.     #[verus_spec(result =>
335.         requires
336.             phys_view().initialized,
337.             phys_view().inv(),
338.         ensures
339.             phys_view().inv(),
340.             phys_view().initialized,
341.             match result {
342.                 Ok(frame) => {
343.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
344.                     &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
345.                 },
346.                 Err(_) => true,
347.             },
348.     )]
349.     pub fn alloc_kernel_frame(&mut self) -> Result<KernelFrame, Error> {
350.         let frame_addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc()?;
351.         KernelFrame::new(frame_addr).inspect_err(|e| {
352.             warn!("failed to wrap frame after KernelFrame::new failure: {e:?}");
353.             if let Err(free_err) = frame::free(frame_addr) {
354.                 warn!("failed to free frame after KernelFrame::new failure: {free_err:?}");
355.             }
356.         })
357.     }
358. 
359.     ///
360.     /// # Description
361.     ///
362.     /// Allocates a contiguous range of kernel frames into caller-provided storage.
363.     ///
364.     /// Kernel stacks require physically contiguous frames because the kernel uses identity
365.     /// mapping and the hardware stack pointer traverses the region linearly.
366.     /// Kernel allocations bypass the watermark — no artificial ceiling.
367.     ///
368.     /// # Parameters
369.     ///
370.     /// - `count`: Number of frames to allocate.
371.     /// - `frames`: Mutable reference to a pre-allocated vector into which to store
372.     ///   those frames' addresses.
373.     ///
374.     /// # Return Values
375.     ///
376.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned and `frames` is filled with `count`
377.     /// contiguous entries. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
378.     ///
379.     // Trusted shim: allocates a physically-contiguous run from the global allocator
380.     // (bypassing the watermark) and wraps each frame, with a two-phase
381.     // (`Vec::clear` + `frame::free`) rollback Verus cannot body-verify without
382.     // editing exec code. On success exactly `count` frames are handed out, each now
383.     // allocated, and their base addresses form an ascending page-stride run
384.     // (contiguity is load-bearing for kernel stacks). On error the vector is emptied.
385.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
386.     #[verus_spec(result =>
387.         requires
388.             phys_view().initialized,
389.             phys_view().inv(),
390.             old(frames)@.len() == 0,
391.         ensures
392.             phys_view().inv(),
393.             phys_view().initialized,
394.             match result {
395.                 Ok(()) => {
396.                     &&& final(frames)@.len() == count
397.                     &&& forall|i: int|
398.                         0 <= i < count as int ==>
399.                             #[trigger] phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
400.                     &&& exists|base: int|
401.                         #[trigger] kernel_frames_contiguous(final(frames)@, base)
402.                 },
403.                 Err(_) => final(frames)@.len() == 0,
404.             },
405.     )]
406.     pub fn alloc_many_kernel_frames(
407.         &mut self,
408.         count: usize,
409.         frames: &mut Vec<KernelFrame>,
410.     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
411.         // Check if caller-provided vector is not empty.
412.         if !frames.is_empty() {
413.             let reason: &str = "frames vector is not empty";
414.             error!("{reason}");
415.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
416.         }
417.         if frames.capacity() < count {
418.             let reason: &str = "frames vector has insufficient capacity";
419.             error!("{reason}");
420.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
421.         }
422. 
423.         let base_addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc_contiguous(count)?;
424.         let base_raw: usize = base_addr.into_raw_value();
425.         for i in 0..count {
426.             let raw_addr: usize = base_raw + i * mem::PAGE_SIZE;
427.             match FrameAddress::from_raw_value(raw_addr).and_then(KernelFrame::new) {
428.                 Ok(kf) => frames.push(kf),
429.                 Err(e) => {
430.                     // Drop already-wrapped frames (frees them via KernelFrame::Drop).
431.                     frames.clear();
432.                     // Free remaining un-wrapped frames from the contiguous allocation.
433.                     for j in i..count {
434.                         let leak_raw: usize = base_raw + j * mem::PAGE_SIZE;
435.                         if let Ok(fa) = FrameAddress::from_raw_value(leak_raw) {
436.                             if let Err(e) = frame::free(fa) {
437.                                 warn!("failed to free leaked frame {fa:?}: {e:?}");
438.                             }
439.                         }
440.                     }
441.                     return Err(e);
442.                 },
443.             }
444.         }
445.         Ok(())
446.     }
447. }

4. // PhysMemoryManager - Specifications
5. //
6. // `PhysMemoryManager` is a *stateless* facade over the global frame allocator
7. // (`Upool` carries no fields; kernel frames are drawn directly from `frame::*`).
8. // It therefore has no per-instance abstract state of its own: the caller-relevant
9. // state is the global frame-reservation state, modelled by the do-not-modify
10. // `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView` in `mod.spec.rs`. All manager contracts are
11. // stated over `phys_view()` and the returned frame values -- exactly the monotone
12. // style used by the `frame::*` free-function shims (`book`, `alloc_range`, ...).
13. //
14. // See `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-manager/view_design.md` for why a bespoke
15. // `self@` View is *not* realizable here (a constant view cannot witness global
16. // mutation, and there is no `old(phys_view())`).
17. 
18. verus! {
19. 
20. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
21. use crate::mm::phys::{
22.     phys_view,
23.     FrameAllocView,
24. };
25. use vstd::seq::Seq;
26. 
27. /// The kernel watermark threshold, lifted to `int`.
28. ///
29. /// Abstract (uninterpreted) form of the build-time constant
30. /// `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`: the number of physical frames the
31. /// allocator must keep in reserve for kernel use, below which user allocations
32. /// are refused. It is left opaque because the concrete value is a build-time
33. /// constant of an external crate; callers only rely on its consistency, not its
34. /// magnitude.
35. pub uninterp spec fn spec_kernel_watermark() -> int;
36. 
37. /// A user allocation of `count` frames is admissible only if, after servicing it,
38. /// at least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames would still be free.
39. ///
40. /// Stated on the abstract free-set cardinality -- never on an allocator counter --
41. /// so it survives any frame-allocator reimplementation. `free_frames.len()` is
42. /// meaningful because the allocator keeps `free_frames` finite (see the shim
43. /// contracts, which (re)establish `phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite()`).
44. pub open spec fn spec_watermark_ok(v: FrameAllocView, count: int) -> bool {
45.     v.free_frames.len() >= spec_kernel_watermark() + count
46. }
47. 
48. /// `addrs` is an ascending, page-stride-contiguous run of frame addresses based
49. /// at `base`: `addrs[i] == base + i * PAGE_SIZE`.
50. ///
51. /// Used to state the contiguity guarantee of `alloc_many_kernel_frames` over the
52. /// sequence of returned kernel-frame addresses (kernel stacks require a linear,
53. /// identity-mapped physical region).
54. pub open spec fn is_contiguous_run(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int) -> bool {
55.     forall|i: int|
56.         0 <= i < addrs.len() ==> #[trigger] addrs[i] == base + i * spec_page_size()
57. }
58. 
59. /// `frames` is an ascending, page-stride-contiguous run of kernel frames based at
60. /// `base`: the address of the `i`-th frame is `base + i * PAGE_SIZE`.
61. ///
62. /// Phrased directly over the `KernelFrame` sequence (using each frame's abstract
63. /// address `@`) so that the `alloc_many_kernel_frames` contiguity guarantee can be
64. /// triggered without an inline closure (closures are forbidden inside triggers).
65. pub open spec fn kernel_frames_contiguous(frames: Seq<KernelFrame>, base: int) -> bool {
66.     forall|i: int|
67.         0 <= i < frames.len() ==> #[trigger] frames[i]@ == base + i * spec_page_size()
68. }
69.

21.     ensures

37.     ensures

39.             0 <= i < addrs.len() && 0 <= j < addrs.len() && i != j ==> addrs[i] != addrs[j],
40. {
41.     admit();
42. }

 ### `alloc_kernel_frame(&mut self) -> Result<KernelFrame, Error>`
 - **Callers assume (Ok):** one owned `KernelFrame` backed by a real physical frame,
   **bypassing the watermark** (no artificial ceiling — kernel allocations must always
   be servable when memory exists). Callers wrap it in `KernelPage`, optionally
   `clear()` it (frame is not guaranteed zeroed), and build page directories/tables.
 - **Callers assume (Err):** nothing allocated, no leak; the helper already frees the
   raw frame if `KernelFrame::new` fails. Caller propagates via `?`.
 - **Would break callers:** applying the user watermark to kernel allocations (would
   starve page-table/page-directory allocation under memory pressure), or leaking a
   frame when `KernelFrame::new` fails.
 - **Would NOT break callers:** the alloc→wrap→free-on-wrap-failure mechanics are
   internal; callers only need "owned kernel frame or clean error, no watermark."
 
 ### `alloc_many_kernel_frames(&mut self, count, frames: &mut Vec<KernelFrame>) -> Result<(), Error>`
 - **Callers assume (preconditions):** empty `Vec` with capacity ≥ count (validated,
   `InvalidArgument` otherwise). `alloc_kpages` (`virt::manager.rs:748`) enforces this
   itself before calling.
 - **Callers assume (Ok):** `frames` holds exactly `count` **physically contiguous**
   kernel frames (ascending by `PAGE_SIZE`), watermark bypassed. Contiguity is the
   load-bearing guarantee — kernel stacks rely on a linear identity-mapped region.
 - **Callers assume (Err):** all-or-nothing — `frames` cleared, every frame from the
   contiguous block freed (both already-wrapped via `Drop` and not-yet-wrapped via
   explicit `frame::free`), no leaks.
 - **Would break callers:** non-contiguous frames on success, partial fills, or any
   leak on the error path; applying a watermark.
 - **Would NOT break callers:** the base-address + offset wrapping loop and the
   two-phase cleanup are internal details.
 
 ### `check_user_watermark(count) -> Result<(), Error>` (private)
 - **Internal callers** (`alloc_user_frame`, `alloc_many_user_frames`) assume: `Ok`
   iff `free_count() >= KERNEL_WATERMARK + count` (with `count==0` / overflow handled —
   `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count` overflow yields `InvalidArgument`); `Err(OutOfMemory)`
   when the request would drop free frames below the watermark. It is a pure gate with
   no side effects on allocator state.
 - Not part of any external contract; exists only to share the watermark policy between
   the single- and many-frame user paths.
 
 ## Abstract Resource
 `PhysMemoryManager` is the kernel's **single global owner of physical RAM frames**. It
 hands out ownership of individual physical frames in two qualities of service: **user
 frames** (refcounted, watermark-gated, possibly non-contiguous, drawn from `Upool`) and
 **kernel frames** (watermark-exempt, single or physically-contiguous runs, drawn
 directly from the `frame` allocator). Callers care only about: *did I get the exact
 frames I asked for, owned cleanly, with the right contiguity/watermark policy — and on
 failure, is the allocator left untouched with nothing leaked?*
 
 ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
 - **Lifecycle:** usable only after a successful `init`; `init` is one-shot/monotonic
   (second call errors, never clobbers). `get_mut` is valid exactly when initialized.
 - **Ownership / no double-allocation:** each successful allocation yields frames the
   caller exclusively owns; the same physical frame is never handed to two live owners.
   User frames additionally carry refcount semantics for CoW sharing.
 - **All-or-nothing on bulk ops:** `alloc_many_*` either fully succeed (vector holds
   exactly `count`) or fully roll back (vector empty, every interim frame freed). No
   partial states, no leaks.
 - **Policy split:** user allocations are gated by `KERNEL_WATERMARK`
   (`free_count() >= KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`); kernel allocations bypass it entirely.
 - **Contiguity contract:** `alloc_many_kernel_frames` guarantees physical contiguity;
   `alloc_many_user_frames` makes no such promise.
 - **Caller-provided storage discipline:** bulk APIs require an empty, sufficiently
   pre-reserved `Vec`; they validate and reject otherwise (`InvalidArgument`) rather
   than reallocating.
 
 ## Notes for View Design
 - The natural abstract state is already largely present upstream in
   `mm::phys::mod.spec.rs` (`PhysMemView { initialized, frames: FrameAllocView }` with
   `allocated_frames` / `free_frames` / `refcounts`, plus `phys_view()`). These are
   **do-not-modify** existing definitions and form the obvious anchor:
   - `init`'s post-state ↔ `initialized` flips on (`spec_initialize`).
   - `alloc_*` move frames `free → allocated` (refcount → 1) — analogous to
     `spec_book_frame` / `spec_book_frames`, but driven by allocation rather than
     booking.
   - the watermark gate is expressible against `free_frames` cardinality vs.
     `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`.
 - The View must NOT expose `Upool` internals, `MaybeUninit`/`AtomicBool` storage, or
   the loop/cleanup mechanics — no caller observes them. Stick to: initialized flag,
   free/allocated frame sets, refcounts, and the contiguity/watermark policy.

244.

246. |---|---|
247. | **Substitution** | ✅ Each field describes state any frame allocator maintains; none mentions `Upool`/bitmap/atomic storage. |

256. 
257. 1. **`initialized: bool` on the manager View.** Rejected: `init` is static and
258.    the lifecycle is already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` /
259.    `phys_view()`. Holding `&mut PhysMemoryManager` implies initialized, so the
260.    field is a per-instance constant — fails minimality/substitution.
261.

263.    Rejected: it would re-derive exactly `FrameAllocView` + `wf`, fragmenting the
264.    `mm::phys` vocabulary and adding proof overhead, with no caller-visible gain.
265. 
266. 3. **Separate `user_frames` vs. `kernel_frames` allocated sets.** Rejected: the
267.    user/kernel distinction is a *policy on the allocation path* (watermark gate,
268.    contiguity guarantee), not a property of a frame once owned. The watermark is
269.    captured by `spec_watermark_ok`; contiguity by `is_contiguous_run`. Splitting
270.    the set would leak an implementation-irrelevant taxonomy and complicate the
271.    "a frame is allocated to exactly one owner" invariant. Fails substitution.
272. 
273. 4. **`free_count: nat` / `watermark` as View fields.** Rejected: `free_count` is
274.    derivable as `free_frames.len()` (redundant); the watermark is a compile-time
275.    constant (`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`), not state. Modeling either as a
276.    field violates minimality.
277. 
278. 5. **`Upool` / bitmap / `MaybeUninit`+`AtomicBool` storage in the View.**
279.    Rejected outright: no caller observes these; they are exactly the "HOW" the
280.    abstraction must hide. Fails substitution and caller-only.
281. 
282. 6. **A `contiguous: bool` flag in the View.** Rejected: contiguity is a property
283.    of a *specific returned run* at a call site, not a standing property of the
284.    manager's state. It belongs in `alloc_many_kernel_frames`'s `ensures` via
285.    `is_contiguous_run`, not in the View.
286.

 initialized; every later `get_mut()`/`alloc_*` is valid" — is a property of the
 **subsystem**, already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView { initialized,
 frames }` and `phys_view()` (`spec_initialize` flips `initialized` on).
 
 A caller that *holds* a `&mut PhysMemoryManager` is, by construction, past
 `init`; per-instance the flag is a constant `true` and carries no information.
 By the **substitution + minimality** tests an `initialized` field on the manager
 View would be dead, so it is excluded. `init` is `external_body` (TCB-allowed via
 `get_mut`/lifecycle reasoning) and states its post-condition over `phys_view()`,
 not over `self@`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Well-formedness Invariant
 
 ```rust
 impl PhysMemoryManager {
     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
         // Frame-allocator well-formedness: page-alignment, allocated/free
         // disjointness, allocated <-> positive-refcount consistency, free
         // frames have no refcount, refcounts in 1..=255.
         &&& self@.wf()
         // Cardinalities must be finite so the watermark predicate can speak of
         // free_frames.len(). (Set::len is only meaningful on finite sets.)
         &&& self@.allocated_frames.finite()
         &&& self@.free_frames.finite()
     }
 }
 ```
 
 `wf()` is reused verbatim from `FrameAllocView::wf` (do-not-modify). The two
 `finite()` conjuncts are the only abstraction-level additions, and they exist
 solely because the watermark policy is stated over `free_frames.len()` (below);
 without finiteness `.len()` is undefined.
 
 `view()` is `closed`, `inv()` is `open` — matching the project rule that the
 abstraction mapping stays hidden while the invariant is visible to callers.
 
 ---
 
 ## Spec Transition Functions & Policy Predicates
 
 `FrameAllocView` is frozen, so manager-scoped helpers are declared as free
 `spec fn`s in `manager.spec.rs` (they *consume/produce* `FrameAllocView`; they do
 not extend its definition). These are the vocabulary the six target functions'
 `requires`/`ensures` will be written in.
 
 ### Allocation = move free → allocated, refcount 1
 
 The caller-observable effect of *every* successful single-frame allocation
 (user or kernel) is identical: one frame leaves `free_frames`, enters
 `allocated_frames`, gains refcount `1`. (Watermark is a *gate*, not part of the
 post-state; contiguity is a property of the returned addresses, below.)
 
 ```rust
 /// Post-state of allocating one previously-free frame `addr`.
 pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frame(v: FrameAllocView, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
     FrameAllocView {
         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
         free_frames:      v.free_frames.remove(addr),
         refcounts:        v.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
     }
 }
 
 /// Post-state of allocating a whole set of previously-free frames at once,
 /// each with refcount 1. (Bulk user/kernel allocation.)
 pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frames(v: FrameAllocView, fs: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
     FrameAllocView {
         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.union(fs),
         free_frames:      v.free_frames.difference(fs),
         refcounts:        v.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
                               Map::new(|a: int| fs.contains(a), |a: int| 1int)),
     }
 }
 ```
 
 These deliberately mirror the existing `PhysMemView::spec_book_frame` /
 `spec_book_frames` shapes (allocation and booking have the same abstract effect),
 keeping the whole `mm::phys` module in one transition vocabulary. The
 "all-or-nothing" bulk contract is captured by stating the success post-state as
 `spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)` and the error post-state as `self@ == old(self)@`
 (frame condition) — no partial-fill state is expressible, which is exactly the
 caller guarantee.
 
 ### Watermark policy (user path only)
 
 ```rust
 /// User allocations are admissible iff servicing `count` frames still leaves at
 /// least KERNEL_WATERMARK frames free. Stated on the abstract free-set size, not
 /// on any allocator counter.
 pub open spec fn spec_watermark_ok(v: FrameAllocView, count: int) -> bool {
     v.free_frames.len() >= (config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK as int) + count
 }
 ```
 
 - `alloc_user_frame` / `alloc_many_user_frames` succeed only when
   `spec_watermark_ok(self@, count)`; on `!spec_watermark_ok` they fail with
   `OutOfMemory` and leave `self@` unchanged.
 - `check_user_watermark(count)` is exactly the decision procedure for this
   predicate (plus an `InvalidArgument` arm when `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`
   overflows `usize`); it is the shared private gate, no state effect.
 - `alloc_kernel_frame` / `alloc_many_kernel_frames` are specified **without**
   this predicate — kernel allocations bypass the watermark.
 
 ### Contiguity (kernel bulk path only)
 
 Contiguity is a property of the **returned addresses**, not a View field. Using
 the observable address accessors (`KernelFrame::base()`, `UserFrame::address()`),
 the kernel bulk contract is stated over the returned sequence:
 
 ```rust
 /// `addrs` is an ascending, page-stride contiguous run of length `n`.
 pub open spec fn is_contiguous_run(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int) -> bool {
     forall|i: int| 0 <= i < addrs.len()
         ==> addrs[i] == base + i * spec_page_size()
 }
 ```
 
 - `alloc_many_kernel_frames` ensures the returned frames' base addresses satisfy
   `is_contiguous_run(.., base)` for some `base`, and that this run is precisely
   the set moved free→allocated in `spec_alloc_frames`.
 - `alloc_many_user_frames` makes **no** contiguity claim (its `count` frames are
   just *some* set moved free→allocated) — matching "non-contiguity is explicitly
   fine."
 
 ---
 
 ## Mapping to Verification-Order Targets
 
 | Function | Abstract effect over `self@` |
 |---|---|
 | `init` (static, TCB) | establishes subsystem; stated over `phys_view().spec_initialize(..)`, **not** `self@`. |
 | `alloc_user_frame` | `requires`-able success when `spec_watermark_ok(self@,1)`; `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frame(old, a)`, returned `UserFrame.address()@ == a`, `a ∈ old.free_frames`. `Err` ⇒ `self@` unchanged. |
 | `alloc_many_user_frames` | preconds: `frames` empty, `capacity ≥ count`. `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)`, `|fs| == count`, `frames` holds exactly those addrs, watermark held. `Err` ⇒ `frames` empty & `self@` unchanged. |
 | `check_user_watermark` | pure: `Ok` ⇔ `spec_watermark_ok(self@, count)` (no overflow); no effect. |
 | `alloc_kernel_frame` | `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frame(old, a)`, returned `KernelFrame.base()@ == a`; **no** watermark gate. `Err` ⇒ unchanged. |
 | `alloc_many_kernel_frames` | `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)`, the addrs form `is_contiguous_run(.., base)`, `|fs| == count`; **no** watermark. `Err` ⇒ `frames` empty & `self@` unchanged. |
 
 ---
 
 ## Design Rationale (per field — substitution test)
 
 | Element | Why needed | Substitution test ("rewrite with a different algorithm?") |
 |---|---|---|
 | `allocated_frames: Set<int>` | Callers must know a successful alloc yields a frame *not already owned* (no double-allocation); bulk/contiguity contracts name the moved set. | ✅ Any frame allocator — bitmap, free-list, buddy — has a notion of "currently handed-out frames." Survives. |
 | `free_frames: Set<int>` | Source of new allocations; the watermark policy is stated over its cardinality. | ✅ Every allocator distinguishes available capacity; representation-independent. Survives. |
 | `refcounts: Map<int,int>` | User frames are refcounted for CoW sharing; callers rely on "freshly allocated ⇒ refcount 1" and on the allocated⇔positive-refcount law. | ✅ Refcounting is a *caller-facing* QoS property of user frames, not a storage choice; any impl that supports CoW exposes it. Survives. |
 | `inv := wf() ∧ finite` | Reuses proven frame-allocator law; finiteness makes `free_frames.len()` (watermark) well-defined. | ✅ Pure properties of the abstract sets/map; independent of allocator internals. |
 
 The transition helpers (`spec_alloc_frame`, `spec_alloc_frames`),
 `spec_watermark_ok`, and `is_contiguous_run` are all phrased over abstract
 `Set`/`Seq`/`int` and the public `spec_page_size`/`KERNEL_WATERMARK` constants —
 each survives a complete reimplementation because each restates *what* the
 operation guarantees, never *how* it is computed.
 
 ---
 
 ## Quality Review
 
 | Criterion | Result |
 |---|---|
 | **Substitution** | ✅ Each field describes state any frame allocator maintains; none mentions `Upool`/bitmap/atomic storage. |
 | **Caller-only** | ✅ Allocated/free/refcount are precisely what `vmem`/`virt::manager` reason about; no internal bookkeeping exposed. |
 | **Complete** | ✅ Covers ownership/no-double-alloc (`allocated_frames`), watermark (`free_frames.len()`), CoW (`refcounts`), all-or-nothing (`spec_alloc_frames` + frame condition), contiguity (`is_contiguous_run`), lifecycle (delegated to `phys_view`). |
 | **Minimal** | ✅ Three fields, each used by ≥1 target's spec; `initialized` deliberately excluded as per-instance-constant. |
 | **No code-as-spec** | ✅ Transitions are set/map algebra; the loop-and-push and two-phase cleanup mechanics are never modeled. |
 
 ---
 
 ## Rejected Alternatives
 
 1. **`initialized: bool` on the manager View.** Rejected: `init` is static and
    the lifecycle is already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` /
    `phys_view()`. Holding `&mut PhysMemoryManager` implies initialized, so the
    field is a per-instance constant — fails minimality/substitution.
 
 2. **A bespoke `PhysManagerView` newtype duplicating allocated/free/refcounts.**
    Rejected: it would re-derive exactly `FrameAllocView` + `wf`, fragmenting the
    `mm::phys` vocabulary and adding proof overhead, with no caller-visible gain.
 
 3. **Separate `user_frames` vs. `kernel_frames` allocated sets.** Rejected: the
    user/kernel distinction is a *policy on the allocation path* (watermark gate,
    contiguity guarantee), not a property of a frame once owned. The watermark is
    captured by `spec_watermark_ok`; contiguity by `is_contiguous_run`. Splitting
    the set would leak an implementation-irrelevant taxonomy and complicate the
    "a frame is allocated to exactly one owner" invariant. Fails substitution.
 
 4. **`free_count: nat` / `watermark` as View fields.** Rejected: `free_count` is
    derivable as `free_frames.len()` (redundant); the watermark is a compile-time
    constant (`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`), not state. Modeling either as a
    field violates minimality.
 
 5. **`Upool` / bitmap / `MaybeUninit`+`AtomicBool` storage in the View.**
    Rejected outright: no caller observes these; they are exactly the "HOW" the
    abstraction must hide. Fails substitution and caller-only.
 
 6. **A `contiguous: bool` flag in the View.** Rejected: contiguity is a property
    of a *specific returned run* at a call site, not a standing property of the
    manager's state. It belongs in `alloc_many_kernel_frames`'s `ensures` via
    `is_contiguous_run`, not in the View.

    phys_view().initialized,

            &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
